desc: Parse H, W and each length-W binary string into an integer bitmask, counting how many rows share each mask.
Prove row flips commute with column flips and that, for a fixed column mask, each row's optimal contribution depends only on popcount(row_mask xor column_mask).
Formulate the total cost as a minimum over all W-bit column masks using the row-mask frequency table.
Derive an efficient algorithm using the W <= 18 bound via Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (XOR convolution).
Implement the Walsh-Hadamard transform (XOR convolution) approach, using the Krawtchouk polynomial to obtain FWHT(g) without a third transform.
Verify the implementation against the three samples (all passed), plus edge case W=1 and the numpy int64 overflow bound.
